items.text: Treats the requested save offer as a proposed solution and restates the ask as a problem to solve (how to keep subscribers the business is losing), including what is not part of the problem.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Puts a value on the problem (for example revenue or subscribers lost per month to failed payments) so the cost of each option can be weighed against it.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: States the recommended test as a hypothesis: the change, the outcome it should move, and the assumption behind it, so the result can confirm or refute it.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How to set performance metrics for your service, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/measuring-success/how-to-set-performance-metrics-for-your-service (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Looks at the loss by segment (plan, tenure, payment method or provider) rather than one overall average, or names segmentation as the next analysis.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How to set performance metrics for your service, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/measuring-success/how-to-set-performance-metrics-for-your-service (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Says what result would mean stopping or not building the save offer, and treats stopping as a valid outcome rather than a failure.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Combines analytics with qualitative evidence (interviews, support tickets) and says where they agree or conflict, rather than relying on one source.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How to set performance metrics for your service, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/measuring-success/how-to-set-performance-metrics-for-your-service (OGL-3.0)

weakAnswers: Build the cancellation save offer with a discount for anyone who clicks cancel.
Price is the main reason people leave, because the survey says so.
Run an A/B test of discount sizes and pick the winner.
Improve onboarding and engagement to reduce churn in general.

items.text: Separates hard constraints (the contractual date and contractual scope) from soft ones (leadership preferences, internal process) and treats them differently in the cut.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Plans the next sprints in detail and later work at a high level, and says the plan will be revisited as the team learns, rather than fixing every sprint up front.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, Planning in agile, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/planning-agile (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Ties the MVP to a small set of objectives with measurable results, so stakeholders can tell whether the launch scope does what it is meant to.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, Planning in agile, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/planning-agile (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Makes cross-team or third-party dependencies visible in the plan and names who owns each, not only the dependencies inside the backlog file.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, Planning in agile, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/planning-agile (OGL-3.0)

items.text: With a fixed deadline, frames the roadmap around what can be delivered by that date and states what moves to after launch and when it is next reviewed.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, Planning in agile, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/planning-agile (OGL-3.0)

weakAnswers: Ask the team to work harder or add overtime to fit everything in.
Keep every must-have and hope velocity improves.
Cut the lowest-priority items until the points fit, without checking dependencies or the contract.
Move the launch date.

items.text: Treats "redesign onboarding" as a proposed solution and restates the ask as the problem of people not completing signup, before choosing what to change.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Puts a size on the problem (signups or customers lost per week since the change) so the effort of each option can be weighed against it.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Reads the drop against the weekly trend before and after the change rather than one before/after snapshot, and says what else changed in the same weeks.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How to set performance metrics for your service, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/measuring-success/how-to-set-performance-metrics-for-your-service (OGL-3.0)

items.text: States the recommended fix as a hypothesis (the change, the outcome it should move, the assumption) with a result that would show it was wrong.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How to set performance metrics for your service, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/measuring-success/how-to-set-performance-metrics-for-your-service (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Uses user-reported evidence (reviews, support contacts) to confirm or question what the funnel numbers suggest, and says where they agree.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How to set performance metrics for your service, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/measuring-success/how-to-set-performance-metrics-for-your-service (OGL-3.0)

weakAnswers: Redesign the onboarding screens to make them simpler and shorter.
Signups fell because of the analytics outage, so nothing really changed.

Run a round of user interviews before deciding anything.

items.text: Treats "a proper search engine" as a proposed solution and restates the ask as the problem of customers not finding parts, including what is out of scope.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Normalises part numbers once when they are stored (an indexed canonical key) and applies the same rule to the query, rather than cleaning text differently in each query.
items.source: PostgreSQL documentation, 12.1 Introduction (full text search), https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/textsearch-intro.html (PostgreSQL Licence)

items.text: Names the database's own full-text search (preprocessed, indexed documents with ranking) as a middle option for the smaller share of real text queries, before a separate engine.
items.source: PostgreSQL documentation, 12.1 Introduction (full text search), https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/textsearch-intro.html (PostgreSQL Licence)

items.text: Notes why the current pattern-matching search falls short for text queries (no ranking, no index support, no handling of word forms), so the text-search share is not ignored.
items.source: PostgreSQL documentation, 12.1 Introduction (full text search), https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/textsearch-intro.html (PostgreSQL Licence)

items.text: Measures part-number lookups and text queries as separate segments with their own baselines, rather than one overall success rate.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How to set performance metrics for your service, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/measuring-success/how-to-set-performance-metrics-for-your-service (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Weighs the ongoing cost of a new service (a second store to keep in sync, reindexing, on-call) against the size of the problem, not only the purchase price.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

weakAnswers: Buy a hosted search engine; the current search is old.
Add fuzzy matching to every query.
Train customers and support staff to type part numbers correctly.
Add more synonyms to the search.

items.text: States the hypothesis the pricing change was meant to test and judges the result against it, rather than against whichever metric moved.
items.source: GOV.UK, A/B testing: comparative studies (Evaluating digital health products), https://www.gov.uk/guidance/ab-testing-comparative-studies (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Says whether the test had enough users and ran long enough for the expected change, and sets sample size and duration before the repeat test starts.
items.source: GOV.UK, A/B testing: comparative studies (Evaluating digital health products), https://www.gov.uk/guidance/ab-testing-comparative-studies (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Names outcomes the test did not measure that the change could harm (for example satisfaction, support contacts or longer-term retention) and how to watch them after release.
items.source: GOV.UK, A/B testing: comparative studies (Evaluating digital health products), https://www.gov.uk/guidance/ab-testing-comparative-studies (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Checks whether the difference is statistically significant, or says the evidence is inconclusive, before calling a winner.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How to set performance metrics for your service, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/measuring-success/how-to-set-performance-metrics-for-your-service (OGL-3.0)

weakAnswers: Variant B won on paid conversion, so roll it out.

The test is flawed, so drop the pricing change entirely.

items.text: Weighs what each option costs to build and run against the value it brings, not the value side alone.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Ties the choice to the quarter's objectives and the measurable results those objectives name.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, Planning in agile, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/planning-agile (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Says how the chosen feature's success will be measured after release, with a current baseline and a target.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How to set performance metrics for your service, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/measuring-success/how-to-set-performance-metrics-for-your-service (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Combines usage data with what customers and support say, and notes where the sources disagree.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How to set performance metrics for your service, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/measuring-success/how-to-set-performance-metrics-for-your-service (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Says when the choice will be revisited and what would make the team switch to another option.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, Planning in agile, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/planning-agile (OGL-3.0)
